title: Micro-sprint Triage Battlecard + Narrative Notes (WIP)
body:
Purpose:
Short, consumable battlecard and narrative kit for SEs and sellers to run 20–40 minute rescue sprints when a pilot hits economic or latency pushback. This is intentionally lightweight — slide titles, one-liner hooks, 3 prioritized rebuttals, a compact ROI snippet, and two canned customer scenarios with speaker notes.

Audience and when to use:
- Use when a pilot is at risk in first 30 days due to latency, cost surprises, or platform integration friction.
- Intended for platform sellers, solution engineers, and SEs.

One-line value prop (for top of slide):
"Keep product UX live and cost-predictable — triage pilots in under an hour with fallbacks that preserve user experience."

Suggested slide / card order (each card = one slide or one page on a one-pager):
1) Sprint header + objective (1 sentence): "Triage: Fix latency or cost blockers so the pilot remains live and we gather usage signals."
2) Quick diagnostics checklist (30–60s): metrics to ask for (p99, avg latency, token mix, request rate, top prompt types, error ratio)
3) Fast fallback ladder (operational playbook) — prioritized: A) Route to compatible lower-latency model variant B) Apply short-ttl prefix cache for repetitive prompts C) Reduce max_tokens or streaming chunking D) Enable quantized instance for Dedicated E) Time-windowed batching during peak bursts
4) Customer impact map (2-min narrative): pair each fallback with expected UX delta and cost delta
5) Top 3 rebuttals (talk tracks) with examples
6) Rapid ROI math (2 numbers): estimate monthly burn saved by fallback x incremental UX impact
7) Two canned scenarios + speaker notes (walkthroughs)

Quick diagnostics checklist (copyable):
- Platform: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
- Model name + pinned version
- Request distribution: median tokens in prompt / completion, % of streaming vs full response
- Latency percentiles: p50 / p90 / p99
- Token spend last 7 days and number of unique active users
- Error / timeout events and stack traces (if any)

Fast fallback ladder (why ordered this way):
- Route to compatible variant: Minimal infra change, immediate effect on latency, keeps developer experience same.
- Short-ttl prefix cache: Great for repetitive prompts (firmography, static templates). Preserves UX for repeated queries.
- Reduce max_tokens or stream chunking: Acceptable UX tradeoff for large completions; easy toggle in prompt config.
- Quantized instance / lower-cost Dedicated profile: Longer-term but large unit-cost wins. Needs ops handshake.
- Time-windowed batching: For sustained throughput bursts — reduces per-token cost but adds headroom to latency SLOs.

Top 3 rebuttals (concise):
1) "Switching to a lower-latency variant will be nearly invisible for 80% of your queries" — show example prompt and example outputs side-by-side.
2) "Short TTL caching targets repeated lookups — for your 3 highest-frequency templates we estimate 30–50% token reduction" — one-line math: 10k daily requests * 150 tokens average * 40% reduction = ~600k tokens/day saved.
3) "We can stage a Dedicated quantized instance behind a feature flag in a week and measure cost delta using canary traffic" — quick rollout plan and rollback bullet.

Rapid ROI snippet (copyable):
- Input: 15k daily queries, avg 200 tokens total, hosted egress cost $0.000X per token (placeholder).
- Fallback plan A (variant routing) expected cost delta: -25% unit cost -> monthly savings = (15k * 200 * 0.75 * 30) * unit_cost_diff.
- Fallback plan B (cache top 3 templates): expected token reduction 30% on those requests -> incremental monthly savings estimate included on slide.
(Replace unit_cost placeholders with pricing from account billing prior to sending customer-facing numbers.)

Canned scenario A: "Customer: Insurance form summarization pilot — intermittent timeouts at 200 concurrent users"
- Symptoms: p99 spikes to 1.8s, some dropped completions during peak, customer concerned about UX for claims agents.
- Suggested triage sequence: 1) Route non-critical summarization to faster variant for agent view only (canary 10%) 2) Short TTL cache for repeated policy lookups 3) Drop max_tokens for background batch jobs
- Speaker notes: Lead with empathy — "we want to keep agents productive now; we'll make the model switch invisible for them while we measure quality." Show before/after token counts and an expected latency delta.

Canned scenario B: "Customer: Embedded support assistant — pilot spike creates unpredictable cost; finance flagged monthly burn"
- Symptoms: High completion lengths for conversation threads, cost overshoot >20% vs forecast.
- Suggested triage sequence: 1) Enforce response length budget with progressive truncation + user prompt hinting 2) Enable sampling/temperature cap to reduce hallucination re-generations 3) For Dedicated customers: propose a short-term quantized slot to demonstrate 30–40% cost reduction
- Speaker notes: Use cost-as-productivity metric: "We want to ensure the assistant survives scale without degrading product-market fit; here’s how we conserve run-rate while preserving core value."

Suggested one-liners for outreach/email subject lines:
- "30-min triage to keep your pilot live — quick options inside"
- "Pilot rescue: three changes that reduce avg latency and monthly spend"

Objection handling snippets (short):
- "Quality will drop" -> "We'll canary 10% of traffic and provide side-by-side sample diff; rollback instantly if quality delta exceeds your threshold."
- "Ops changes are heavy" -> "Most tactics are config toggles or routing rules; Dedicated changes are an ops conversation with a 1-week runway for canary."
- "We need exact numbers" -> "We’ll run a 48-hour controlled canary and deliver a short report with pXX latency and cost delta — no long-term commitment."

Checklist for post-sprint follow-up (what SE sends after 30–60m triage):
- Short summary of actions taken and exact toggles with timestamps
- Before/after key metrics (p50/p90/p99 latency, token spend, failure counts) for the 48h window
- Plan for final resolution: pilot config changes to keep, engineering tasks to schedule, and suggested contract milestone to re-evaluate
- Next meeting slot proposed: 7–10 days

Open questions we should standardize in docs (for team backlog):
- A standard set of sample side-by-side outputs to show quality delta between primary/variant models for top 5 prompt archetypes.
- A templated canary report format (metrics + screenshots) that SEs can auto-fill.
- Better visibility in Console for per-prompt token breakdown during pilot (feature request).

Quick production notes for content pack (assets to assemble):
- 6 one-slide cards: header, diagnostics, fallbacks, impact map, rebuttals, follow-up checklist
- 2x sample side-by-side output snippets per common archetype (FAQ, summarization, rerank)
- Templated email and Slack snippets for pilot owner outreach
- Short how-to for enabling routing policies in Console and for toggling prefix caching

Next steps (owner + ETA):
- Maya T. to author first slide pack and sample outputs (ETA: 3 working days)
- Omar R. to draft canary report template and link to metrics queries (ETA: 1 week)
